findings.title: Reschedule flow still immediately cancels SendGrid-scheduled email reminders, reintroducing the exact bug this PR fixes
findings.body: In the reschedule branch, deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`), which calls the SendGrid '/v3/user/scheduled_sends' cancel endpoint synchronously instead of deferring to the new `cancelled` flag + CRON mechanism. The whole point of this PR is that immediate SendGrid cancellation can fail once the account hits the 100-pending-cancellations limit, silently letting the old reminder email go out. By keeping immediateDelete=true specifically for rescheduled bookings (the scenario explicitly named in the PR title), this path is not actually fixed: under load, rescheduled-booking reminder emails can still be sent even though they were supposed to be cancelled. Other call sites (handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx requestReschedule) correctly omit the third argument so cancellation is deferred.

findings.title: Immediate-delete branch never deletes or updates the WorkflowReminder DB row, leaking orphan records
findings.body: When deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true and a referenceId, the function calls SendGrid to cancel the batch and then returns, without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or marking it cancelled. For call sites where the parent record isn't deleted via cascade afterwards (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts's reschedule flow, which does not delete the original booking or its reminders), this leaves a permanently 'scheduled: true' WorkflowReminder row in the database that is never updated. It will only eventually get swept up by scheduleEmailReminders.ts's blanket 'scheduledDate <= now' deleteMany once its date has passed, meaning stale/incorrect reminder records persist for potentially days.

findings.title: remindersToCancel query lacks a method filter, risking SendGrid API misuse on non-email reminders
findings.body: The `remindersToCancel` query filters only by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, without restricting `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` (unlike the deleteMany cleanup query above it and the unscheduledReminders query below it, both of which filter by method). The subsequent loop unconditionally sends every matched reminder's `referenceId` to the SendGrid `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel endpoint as a `batch_id`. If an SMS WorkflowReminder is ever marked `cancelled: true` (currently not done by the SMS manager, but nothing in the schema or type system prevents it), its Twilio SID would be sent to SendGrid, which would fail or behave unpredictably, and the record would still be deleted from the DB as if it had been properly cancelled via Twilio.

findings.title: A single failed cancellation aborts the whole cancellation batch, leaving earlier successes undeleted
findings.body: The entire cancel loop (SendGrid request + collecting delete promises) is wrapped in one try/catch, and the collected `workflowRemindersToDelete` are only awaited after the for-loop completes. If the SendGrid cancel request throws for any single reminder mid-loop, the exception propagates out of the loop before `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is reached, so none of the already-successfully-cancelled reminders processed earlier in the same run get their DB rows deleted. This causes redundant repeat cancellation calls on the next CRON run and delays cleanup, and masks partial failures since only one generic console.log is emitted for the whole batch.

findings.title: Workflow deletion still cancels all scheduled email reminders immediately instead of deferring
findings.body: In the `delete` mutation, scheduled EMAIL reminders are cancelled with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` (immediateDelete=true), issuing an immediate SendGrid cancel call for every reminder instead of using the new deferred `cancelled` flag mechanism this PR introduces to avoid the SendGrid pending-cancellations limit. For a popular workflow with many active bookings and scheduled reminders, deleting it could still trigger the same 100-pending-cancellation failure mode described in the PR, silently letting some reminder emails go out despite the workflow being deleted.

findings.title: No automated tests cover the new deferred-cancellation CRON logic
findings.body: This PR introduces the core fix (the `cancelled` flag on WorkflowReminder plus new logic in scheduleEmailReminders.ts to batch-cancel reminders within the next hour), but no tests were added to verify that reminders marked cancelled are correctly filtered by method/date, that the SendGrid cancel call is made with the right batch id, or that DB rows are cleaned up appropriately. Given the bug this PR fixes was itself a silent failure mode (reminders sent despite being 'cancelled'), lack of test coverage for this exact mechanism increases the risk of a future regression going unnoticed.
